title: Why Do I Feel Wired but Tired? What's Happening and How to Come Down

copy.cover_headline: Your eyes are heavy but your mind won't stop

points.headline: Two systems, pulling opposite ways
points.body: Sleep pressure says lie down. Your stress response says stay alert. So you get heavy eyes and a buzzing mind. It's a mismatch between two systems, not a flaw in you.

points.headline: Slow to switch off, not always on
points.body: Research suggests the issue is often a stress response that's slow to settle once triggered. You felt fine at 6 pm, then a work message or a fast feed nudged you up.

points.headline: What keeps you activated
points.body: Late caffeine, work that never quite ends, and stimulating evenings on screens can all keep you wound up after your energy runs out.

points.headline: The 60-second down-shift
points.body: Phone face down, shoulders drop. Breathe in through your nose for 4. Breathe out slowly for 6. Repeat 6 rounds, about one minute. Stop if you feel dizzy or tingly.

points.headline: What it should feel like
points.body: By the third or fourth exhale, many people notice shoulders lower and the jaw unclench. Yawning is common. Your mind may still be busy. You're bringing your body down a notch.

reel_lines: Your body is ready for sleep.
Your stress response didn't get the memo.
A longer exhale helps bring you back down.
copy.instagram_caption:
Tired eyes, buzzing mind: your sleep pressure is high but your stress response is still on.

Try a one-minute down-shift. Put the phone face down, breathe in through your nose for 4, then out slowly for 6. Six rounds, about a minute. Many people notice their shoulders drop and jaw unclench by the third or fourth exhale. Stop if you feel dizzy or tingly.

Full guide: link in bio.
copy.facebook_message:
Heavy eyes, buzzing mind. Feeling wired but tired usually means your sleep pressure is high while your stress response is still switched on. It's a mismatch between two systems, not a flaw in you.

Late caffeine, work that never quite ends, and stimulating evenings on screens can all keep you activated after your energy runs out.

A quick way to come down: put your phone face down, breathe in for 4, out slowly for 6, and repeat six times. It can help you feel calmer in the moment, though it isn't a sleep fix. If it happens most evenings for weeks, check in with a doctor.

Read the full guide for what the evidence says and a one-minute script for the couch.
